product.title: Cleanroom Wipes for Semiconductor Manufacturing
product.intro: Semiconductor fabrication requires the highest standards of contamination control.
body: Semiconductor manufacturing is one of the most contamination-sensitive industries. With feature sizes now measured in nanometers, even a single particle can ruin an entire wafer. Cleanroom wipes play a critical role in maintaining cleanliness standards.

In a typical fab, wipes are used for cleaning wafer handling equipment, removing residues, and maintaining cleanroom surfaces. Wipes must meet strict specifications for particle generation and ionic contamination.

For ISO Class 5 cleanrooms, polyester knitted wipes with laser-sealed edges are standard. These offer extremely low particle generation and excellent chemical resistance to solvents like IPA and acetone.
ESD-safe wipes are important in semiconductor environments where static discharge can damage components. Anti-static treatments prevent charge buildup during wiping.
When selecting wipes for semiconductor applications, consider: particle count per IEST-RP-CC004, ionic extractables, NVR levels, and edge seal quality.

product.title: ESD Wipes Guide: Protecting Sensitive Electronics
product.intro: Electrostatic discharge is a hidden threat in electronics manufacturing.
body: ESD is one of the most common causes of electronic component failure, costing billions annually. ESD wipes prevent static charge buildup during wiping, protecting sensitive components.
In PCB assembly lines, ESD wipes clean solder paste residues, remove flux, and wipe workstations. Anti-static properties ensure no triboelectric charges discharge into sensitive components.
ESD wipes are made from continuous filament polyester or microfiber with integrated anti-static treatment. They dissipate static electricity rather than allowing accumulation.
Key applications include electronics repair stations, semiconductor handling areas, and PCB inspection stations. Use with other ESD measures like wrist straps and grounding mats.
product.tags: ESD wipes, static control, electronics manufacturing

product.title: Polyester vs Microfiber Cleanroom Wipes
product.intro: Choosing between polyester and microfiber depends on your application.
body: Polyester and microfiber wipes have distinct characteristics for different applications. Polyester wipes from continuous filament fibers offer excellent chemical resistance and low particle generation for solvent application.
Microfiber wipes from split polyester and polyamide fibers trap and hold particles more effectively. Microfiber has superior absorbency for fine particle removal.
For ISO Class 5-6 cleanrooms, both materials are appropriate. Polyester is preferred for controlled solvent application, while microfiber excels in final cleaning passes.
Yongxinyuan DS Series uses high-quality polyester+nylon knitted fabric for optimal performance across cleanroom applications.
product.tags: polyester wipes, microfiber wipes, cleanroom comparison

product.title: Laser Cut vs Ultrasonic Cut vs Cold Cut Wipes
product.intro: Edge sealing directly affects particle generation from cleanroom wipes.
body: Edge sealing is critical for cleanroom wipe performance. Three technologies are used: laser cutting, ultrasonic cutting, and cold cutting.
Laser cutting uses a high-energy beam to simultaneously cut and seal edges, creating the tightest seal with virtually zero particle release. Standard for ISO Class 5-6.
Ultrasonic cutting uses high-frequency vibration to fuse fibers, suitable for ISO Class 7-8. Cold cutting is mechanical without sealing, for industrial-grade applications.
Yongxinyuan offers all three methods: laser cut standard for DS Series, ultrasonic as option, and cold cut for KH Series industrial wipes.
product.tags: laser cut, ultrasonic cut, cold cut, edge sealing

product.title: Cleanroom Wiper Packaging Guide
product.intro: The right packaging preserves wipe cleanliness from factory to point of use.
body: Packaging preserves cleanliness from manufacturing to point of use. Different options suit different cleanroom classes and handling requirements.

Poly bag packaging provides basic protection for ISO Class 7-8. Vacuum packaging reduces volume for better cleanliness and logistics. Double bagged with inner and outer layers is standard for ISO Class 5-6.
Bulk packaging is the most cost-effective option for industrial-grade wipes in non-classified environments.
Yongxinyuan offers all packaging options to match your cleanroom requirements.

technical.title: ISO 14644 Cleanroom Classification Guide
technical.intro: Understand cleanroom classifications from Class 1 to Class 9.
body: ISO 14644-1 defines cleanroom classes based on airborne particle concentration. ISO Class 1 is cleanest, Class 9 least strict.
ISO Class 5 permits no more than 3,520 particles at 0.5 microns per cubic meter. Used for semiconductor fabs and aseptic filling.
ISO Class 8 permits up to 3,520,000 particles. Suitable for general cleanroom manufacturing.
Select wipes appropriate for your class. Yongxinyuan DS Series suits ISO Class 5-8 with documented test results.

technical.title: Particle Contamination Control in Semiconductor Manufacturing
technical.intro: Particle contamination is the number one yield killer in semiconductor fabs.
body: Particle contamination is the leading cause of yield loss in semiconductor manufacturing. As devices shrink to 3nm, even smaller particles cause defects.
Sources include operators, equipment wear, process residues, and cleaning materials. Wipes must remove contaminants without introducing new ones.
Wipe particle generation is measured per IEST-RP-CC004. Laser-cut sealed-edge wipes minimize shedding. Ionic contamination is also critical.
Yongxinyuan tests DS Series for both particle generation and ionic extractables.

technical.title: Cleanroom Wiping Procedures and Best Practices
technical.intro: Even the best wipes are ineffective without proper technique.
body: Proper wiping technique is as important as wipe quality. Move contaminants away from surfaces, not spread them.
Wipe in a single direction using the S-fold technique. Change the fold after each pass. Overlap strokes by 10%. Change wipes frequently.
For equipment cleaning, pre-wet with IPA or DI water. Use minimal pressure to avoid generating particles from the surface.
Document procedures in SOPs specifying wipe type, cleaning agent, technique, frequency, and validation.
technical.tags: wiping procedure, cleanroom cleaning, best practices

technical.title: Non-Volatile Residue in Cleanroom Wipes
technical.intro: NVR measures the chemical cleanliness of cleanroom wipes.
body: NVR refers to solid material left after solvent evaporates from a wipe. High NVR leaves residues causing defects in semiconductor and medical device manufacturing.
Testing involves extracting wipes with solvent, evaporating, and weighing residue. Results in mg per gram of material or per square meter.
For ISO Class 5, NVR should be below 0.1 mg/g. Yongxinyuan DS Series maintains tight NVR controls.
Low NVR requires careful raw material selection, controlled manufacturing, and proper packaging.

technical.title: How to Choose Wipes for ISO Class 5-8
technical.intro: Practical guide based on your cleanroom classification and application.
body: Selecting the right wipe for each classification is essential for performance and cost.
For ISO Class 5: laser-sealed edges, documented particle counts, NVR below 0.1 mg/g, double-bagged packaging.
For ISO Class 6-7: ultrasonic-sealed edges acceptable, moderate particle tolerances, standard packaging.
For ISO Class 8: cold-cut or ultrasonic-cut with higher tolerances. Focus on lint-free performance.
Always review batch test reports. Yongxinyuan provides documented results with each production batch.
